How It Works
Condition: Healthy

Organ pairs with mean Otsuka–Ochiai coefficient ≥ 0.001555 per iteration in the healthy literature context. Papers are fetched per organ (two queries per organ: metabolic + hormonal layer) and cross-organ mentions are counted during bootstrapping.

Per-Organ Query (run twice per organ)
(MeSH_ORGAN OR aliases_ORGAN) AND [METABOLIC_FILTER | HORMONAL_FILTER] AND CONDITION_FILTER (Healthy)

In each bootstrap iteration 10% of each organ's paper pool is sampled and cross-organ mentions are counted. A paper only counts as a cross-mention if the two organs' names (or aliases) appear together in the same sentence of its title/abstract. The resulting mean count is then normalized into an Otsuka–Ochiai coefficient:

OO(A, B) = mean cross-mentions √(nA × nB)

so an organ with a much larger literature pool doesn't dominate edges just by volume.

Key Player Scores

Each edge shows metabolites, hormones, and proteins with their bootstrap frequency — the fraction of the 50 iterations in which that molecule was mentioned in the sampled co-occurring papers. A score of 90% means the molecule appeared in 9 out of 10 random samples, indicating consistent literature support.

CV (coefficient of variation): std / mean of the Otsuka–Ochiai coefficient across bootstrap samples. Lower CV = evidence is spread across many papers rather than a few outlier samples.

See bootstrap_overview_healthy.html for the heatmap and full strength ranking.

How papers are selected

Two PubMed queries per organ — one for the metabolic layer and one for the hormonal layer — each ANDing the organ terms with its layer filter, the condition filter, and the crosstalk filter below, fetching up to 50,000 papers each. Papers from both queries are merged per organ; each paper is tagged with the layer(s) it was retrieved from. During bootstrapping, papers from one organ's pool that mention another organ in title/abstract count as cross-organ evidence and drive the stacked bar chart layer breakdown. The mean cross-mention count is then normalized into an Otsuka–Ochiai coefficient using each organ's total literature pool size (n_found) so heavily-studied organs don't dominate purely by volume.

Organ and crosstalk terms are matched as whole words, not substrings — "renal" no longer matches inside "adrenal", so a paper about the adrenal gland can't be mistaken for kidney evidence. A match is also discarded if it's negated — "non-renal", "nonrenal", "non renal", and "not renal" don't count as a positive mention of that organ or crosstalk term.

METABOLIC_FILTER

At least one of these keywords must appear in title or abstract.

metabolism metabolic catabolism anabolism biosynthesis metabolite flux substrate nutrient fuel glucose glucose uptake glycolysis gluconeogenesis energy bioenergetics mitochondria mitochondrial thermogenesis Krebs cycle electron transport oxidation
HORMONAL_FILTER

At least one of these keywords must appear in title or abstract.

hormone hormonal endocrine endocrinology signaling signal transduction insulin glucagon C-peptide amylin somatostatin GLP-1 glucagon-like peptide GIP glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide YY PYY ghrelin cholecystokinin CCK secretin motilin leptin adiponectin resistin visfatin adipsin adipokine thyroid hormone thyroxine triiodothyronine T3 T4 TSH thyroid-stimulating hormone cortisol glucocorticoid mineralocorticoid aldosterone adrenaline epinephrine norepinephrine noradrenaline catecholamine ACTH corticotropin growth hormone IGF-1 insulin-like growth factor testosterone estrogen estradiol progesterone DHEA androgen parathyroid hormone PTH calcitonin vitamin D calcitriol irisin myokine hepatokine FGF21 FGF19 fetuin prolactin oxytocin vasopressin ADH antidiuretic hormone GnRH CRH TRH
CONDITION_FILTER — Healthy

Required by both queries — restricts results to the healthy physiological context.

healthy healthy subjects healthy individuals healthy volunteers healthy adults normal physiology healthy controls
CROSSTALK_FILTER

Required by both queries too — at least one of these keywords must also appear somewhere in the document (a coarse pre-filter), restricting results to papers actually discussing inter-organ relationships, not just papers that happen to mention an organ and a metabolic/hormonal term without relating them to anything else. After fetching, papers are filtered further: kept only if the organ's own name/alias and one of these crosstalk terms appear together in the same sentence of the title/abstract, not merely somewhere in the same document.

network interplay cross-talk crosstalk connection axis inter-organ interorgan cross-organ communication bidirectional feedback loop signaling regulation mediates modulates interaction link coupling cross-regulation pathway

What This Shows

This visualization compares the Healthy Literature-Based Network against the Reference Metabolic Network, which is based on the partial correlation network of healthy subjects (n= 241) with BMI above 24.4 kg/m^2. In this case 35 predefined organ-pair edges.

The counts and lists below are a at the elbow-suggested Otsuka-Ochiai threshold.

Edge Legend
Shared — in both networks (25 edges)
Only in Healthy Literature-Based Network — robust in bootstrap, not a predefined reference edge (11 edges)
Only in Reference — predefined edge with papers, below Healthy Otsuka–Ochiai threshold (10 edges)
Healthy Literature-Based Network Threshold

An edge appears in the Healthy Literature-Based Network when its mean Otsuka–Ochiai coefficient (cross-mention count normalized by each organ's literature pool size) ≥ 0.001555 (across 50 × 10% random samples).
